title: Vendor-hosted supplier document portal described in security marketing language
provenance: Synthetic system authored for this corpus (wayfinder ticket 029). Not derived from, or sanitized from, any real system or any real vendor's datasheet; the marketing phrases are generic and name no product.
notes: Adversarial case 2 of 2, replacing the repair-to-reject case ticket 029 originally specified (see the ticket resolution: that path is unreachable from source text and is already pinned offline by tests/test_pipeline.py). Where case 11 grades silence, this one grades noise dressed as fact. The source is dense with assurance that states nothing verifiable — secure by design, enterprise-grade encryption throughout, fully authenticated and audited, fully compliant — and none of it may set an attribute; it also contradicts itself outright, claiming the nightly extract is encrypted end to end where the runbook says it arrives as a plain CSV, which must resolve to unknown rather than to either side. One genuine control is stated among the noise (vendor-issued username and password on supplier sign-in) so the case cannot be passed by discarding everything, and one genuine absence is stated (picked up as-is) so grounded findings remain available. Far from the payments exemplar in shape: the trust hand-off is an organizational one into a platform we run no part of and can verify nothing inside, and the availability failure is silent staleness.
